item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Fri Jul 31 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: Home Away from Home: Student Life on Campus — Fri Jul 31, 9:00 AM — HERMAN B WELLS LIBRARY
item.description:
Spanning across four decades—1970s to the 2000s—items including scrapbooks, photographs, student papers, and handbooks demonstrate life on and off campus. From decorating dorm rooms to chasing campus ghosts, students have always found ways to build community and make new memories. This exhibit highlights the student experience and the multitude of ways students found a sense of home, identity and belonging at Indiana University.
Source: IU Bloomington Libraries

item.description:

Saturday Crafternoons are a free event for families, students, and friends of all ages! Activities change monthly.
The Wylie House Museum is open 10am-4pm, Fridays and Saturdays, except holidays. Free guided tours are offered on the hour, every hour with the last tour at 3pm. Check the Wylie House Museum socials and website for updated information, parking, and museum hours.

item.title: Smokey Day — Sat Aug 1, 1:30 PM — Brown County State Park
item.description: Join Brown County State Park naturalists for a day of fun! Smokey Day includes a bike parade, cake, and bounce house. You will also get to learn all about Smokey the Bear and why fire safety is important. After gaining all of your fire safety training, there will be a chance to impress Smokey firsthand with your knowledge and take a photo. SCHEDULE • 9:30am to 11am: Bike Decorating – Meet near the Country Store to decorate your bicycle for Smokey’s Bike Parade! • 11am to 11:30am: Bike Parade – Bring your bike and follow Smokey around the first look of Buffalo Ridge Campground. Meet near the Country Store. • 1pm to 1:30pm: Wildland Firefighting – Join the park naturalist at the Nature Center’s Friends’ Shelter for a discussion about wildfire fighting, hear stories, and look at some of the tools used. • 3pm: Smokey’s Birthday – Join Smokey Bear at the Friends’ Shelter near the Nature Center for cake! • 11:30am to 3:30pm: Woods on Wheels and Smokey’s Bounce House – Come to the Nature Cent

item.title: Rum on the Rocks Beach Party — Sat Aug 1, 7:30 PM — 418 Old State Rd 46
item.description: Dress in your island best and join the Hard Truth crew for Rum on the Rocks, our annual summer festival packed with tropical treats, live music, and beachy bliss. Gates to the Hard Truth on the Rocks terrace will open at 3:30 p.m. on Saturday, Aug. 1, welcoming guests to our landlocked island escape. Mai tais and mojitos, frozen piña coladas and daiquiris, and more festive cocktails will bring tropical flair to the terrace bar alongside special, themed food items like coconut shrimp and island barbecue chicken walking tacos. A whole suckling pig will be roasting on the barbecue while Rich Hardesty and the Swing Rays take the stage through the course of the evening. Guest vendors will be offering airbrush body painting, henna tattoos, and Kona Ice island-style shaved ice. And, of course, we haven’t forgotten the limbo contest. At 6:30 p.m., guests can vie for glory and prizes in this test of flexibility, balance, and showmanship. Tickets for guests aged 13+ are $15 and include event acc

item.title: Mindfulness at the Museum — Thu Aug 6, 2:00 PM — SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART
item.description:
Join us at the museum and mentally recenter by making art or journaling, and make some time to check in with yourself! Join us for a therapist-selected art activity meant to help you feel more balanced and in control. No prior skills needed, just bring your heart and mind. This group meets Thursday from 2–3 p.m., excluding holidays and museum closures. Meetings are held in the Atrium of the Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art. Food and beverages are permitted in the atrium, so participants are welcome to bring lunch.
Source: Eskenazi Museum of Art
